note: v1, written: SLOWER FOREVER. Dub house (the style board's t15 row), the comedown's first step: 124 -> 123 bpm (the ramp in the last 32 bars), C minor (5A). 6:14. The featured illusion is the RISSET DECELERANDO: one bar of rims and a clave played as a Risset rhythm slowing forever (three tempo octaves, each halving over eight bars while the slowest fades out and the fastest fades in). It plays alone under a glass pad in the break, sinks under the full groove in B, and cycles twice as fast in R2 before the bpm really drops in the outro. The ear hears everything slowing for minutes, so the real -1 bpm feels like arriving. Cm9 - Abmaj7 - Gsus(b9) - Fm9 as off-beat house-chord stabs into a dub delay (3/16) whose feedback climbs through the break; their low-pass breathes on a 7-bar LFO, and the hats' high-pass on another. A round sub with phantom harmonics, pumped from the kick. THE STAIR falls (G Eb D C) as the stabs' tops and on the glass in B's second half, and rises (C D Eb G) in the outro to hand t16 its G. The grooves develop halfway (A2: answering stabs and off-16th rims; B2: a harder kick and the falling stair on top). Seams per the mix plan: in over kick, hats and a held C (t14's F minor fifth); out over kick, hats and the sub on G at 123. Master: -11.1 LUFS (the tape's loudness proposal), true peak -1.29 dBTP, levels 100 (pinned run 2). A fast compressor at -15 dB/0.3 ms ahead of the loudness stage stopped its limiter flat-topping the kick (runs 8-43 at -10 dB/1 ms; a soft clip made it worse). compscore seeds 0/11/19/29: 96.694/96.941/94.271/96.454.
